media.title: Three years of remote work taught me that your environment is your productivity. Invested in a proper desk, monitor, and chair this year. Not glamorous. Completely changed my output. 💻
Late night shipping session. There's something meditative about being the only one awake while a deployment goes green. This one took three weeks of work. Worth it. ✨
Reading corner setup for the weekend. 'Thinking in Systems' is changing how I see everything — production incidents, team dynamics, career decisions. Systems thinking is the meta-skill. 📚

Team offsite in Goa. After six months async-first, meeting everyone in person was a reminder that relationships are the foundation of everything else. Build the relationship first, optimize the process second. 🌊
Morning walk before deep work. Non-negotiable. The best ideas don't come at the keyboard. They come when you step away from it. 🌱
Bangalore tech community is something special. Spent the evening at a meetup talking RAG architectures with engineers who are building genuinely hard things. The density of talent here is real. 📸
First pull request merged to a major open source project. Took three rejected PRs to get here. Persistence and listening to maintainer feedback. Open source is the best CS education available. 🚀
New mechanical keyboard. Yes, it matters. When you spend eight hours a day typing, the tools aren't optional. Invest in your craft. ⌨️

Sunday cooking session. Parallel processing applies in the kitchen too. Two dishes running simultaneously, both done in the same time as one would take sequentially. Engineering brain never fully switches off. 👨‍🍳
Six months into learning Rust. The borrow checker is no longer the enemy. It's the colleague who won't let you ship memory bugs. Grateful for it. ⚡
End of year reflection. Three products shipped. One failed fast. One is growing slowly. One exceeded every projection. The failed one taught me the most. Always ship the experiment. 🌟

Conference talk done. Speaking about vector databases and semantic search to a room full of engineers who actually build with these tools is a different energy than most conference talks. Real questions. Real problems. 🎤
Hiking clears the system. Technical problems that felt stuck in the morning look completely different after three hours in the hills. Get outside. The bugs will still be there when you return. 🏔️
Mentorship call number 50 this year. Every one of these conversations teaches me something I didn't know I knew. Teaching is learning in disguise. If you can mentor someone, you should. 🤝
